Restore and maintain the ecological integrity of protected areas and classified forests through the adoption of sustainable "best practicesâ€ in agro-sylvo-pastoral systems for the well-being of local populations.

The project will generate socio-economic benefits by maintaining and improving the resource base on which IPLCs and women in West Mayo-Kebbi, East Mayo-Kebbi, Tandjilé and Fitri depend for their livelihoods (income, food, shelter, medicine). It will respond directly to competing demands on this resource base by advancing informed and inclusive land-use planning in the project area, helping to secure IPLCs' access rights to essential resources and serving as an important learning opportunity on how access rights can be formally recognized and respected by the local land-use planning framework.In the targeted landscapes, the project will also support ILODs, ADCs, NGOs and local associations in establishing planning documents and restoring degraded land to improve yields. The project will support women's groups, youth groups and IPLCs in setting up modern NTFP value chains, notably through micro-subsidies, training and the adoption of sustainable collection guides. In addition, the project will support the sustainable management of fish resources and assist stakeholders in drawing up sustainable fisheries management plans and granting fishing equipment. The project will seek to increase productive and sustainable employment for indigenous and local communities in the project areas. The project aims to generate additional income through the improvement of value chains and the promotion of agroforestry for around 1,000 people (at least 30% of whom will be women). A baseline income survey will be carried out at the start of project implementation. A 10% income increase target has been included in the results framework in the appendix.
